SchedTasks Analyzer — Manual

A single-file, no-install Windows tool for scheduled-task triage: what is registered to run on a host, as whom, launching what — and which of it looks like persistence or lateral movement. It parses the Task Scheduler XML itself, cross-checks it against the registry's TaskCache with Eric Zimmerman's RECmd, and turns both into one scored, filterable view. Part of the DFIR-Windows-Artifact-Finder family.

1  What it answers

Scheduled tasks are one of the most common ways attackers keep access to a Windows host and move between hosts: a task can run as SYSTEM at boot, every few minutes, or exactly once a few minutes after it is pushed from another machine. Windows keeps each task in two places — an XML file under C:\Windows\System32\Tasks and a registration in the SOFTWARE hive under …\Schedule\TaskCache — and attackers increasingly tamper with one and not the other.

The questions: What will run on this host, as which account, from where, and when? Which tasks are not Windows' own? Which launch a script host, pull code from the network or run out of a user-writable folder? Which were hidden, half-deleted, or registered without a file — and when were they created and last run?

It is one .hta file: double-click it and it runs on any Windows box through the built-in mshta.exe. The task XML parser is built in. RECmd is needed only for the registry cross-check and is downloaded on request.

  1. Put SchedTasks-Analyzer.hta anywhere — ideally next to the rest of the toolkit — and double-click it.
  2. Set the input to a host or collection folder: every Windows\System32\Tasks, SysWOW64\Tasks and legacy Windows\Tasks below it is found (Velociraptor and KAPE trees work as-is). A single Tasks folder or a single task file works too.
  3. Check the Target hostname (it names the output folder _Processed\<host>\SchedTasks next to the app) and click Process → analyze.
  4. For the registry cross-check, have RECmd available: it is found next to the app (RECmd\, shared with RECmd-Wrapper), in C:\ZimmermanTools, or fetched with Download RECmd. Without it the XML triage still runs.

3  What it reads, and how

  • Discovery. A directory-only dir /s /b walk finds every Tasks folder under the input — fast, and safe on the very long paths collection trees produce.
  • Staging. Each Tasks folder (and its collection's SOFTWARE hive with .LOG1/.LOG2) is copied with robocopy into a short %TEMP% folder first. Collected task paths routinely exceed 260 characters, names can carry Velociraptor %XX encoding, and evidence is never opened in place. The stage is deleted afterwards.
  • Parsing. Task files are UTF-16 XML. They are parsed with MSXML6 with DTDs prohibited and external resources off — task files are attacker-writable input — and every value is HTML-escaped before display. Files that are not well-formed are salvaged with a regex so the command they would have run is still scored.
  • Everything else in a Tasks folder is reported, not skipped: a non-XML file there is flagged (NOTTASK); a UTF-8 task file is flagged (NOTUTF16) because the scheduler always writes UTF-16; legacy .job files are listed and At<n>.job is flagged (ATJOB).
  • One CSV is written per run (<stamp>_SchedTasks_Output.csv) and the view is always built from that CSV, so reopening it later with Load existing CSV… gives exactly the same scored view.

4  The TaskCache cross-check

Every registered task has a Tree key named after its path (holding its GUID, an index and a security descriptor) and a Tasks\{GUID} key (holding its path, author, a binary copy of its actions, and its created / last-run times). The app sweeps both with RECmd and joins them to the XML by file location — never by the XML's own <URI>, which an attacker can write.

StatusWhat it meansWhy it matters
matchedXML and registration agree.Normal. Adds registered / last-run times and the registry copy of the actions.
xml-onlyA task file with no registration.Dropped by hand, registry cleaned, or the hive copy predates it. XMLONLY
reg-onlyRegistered (Tasks key present) but no XML on disk.Still runs, invisible to anyone reading the Tasks folder. Its actions are decoded from the registry. REGONLY
tree-onlyOnly the Tree key is left — no Tasks key, no XML.A normal delete removes all three. Microsoft leftovers of this shape are routine (STALE, +0); a third-party one is residue of a task removed some other way (TREEONLY) — often all that remains of an attacker's cleaned-up task.
deletedA registration RECmd recovered from hive free space.Shows tasks that were deleted, with their actions where recoverable. REGDELETED

Two more checks run on matched tasks: a Tree key with no SD value is hidden from schtasks and the Task Scheduler UI (the "Tarrask" technique, NOSD), and a registry copy of the actions that differs from the XML is flagged (ACTMISMATCH). A registration whose GUID conflicts with the task that owns a path is kept as its own record rather than merged.

Live machine: Windows keeps the live SOFTWARE hive locked, so This machine runs are XML-only (and need an elevated mshta to read the Tasks folder). Collect the hive, or use RECmd-Wrapper against a shadow copy.

5  Timestamps you can trust

Task files extracted from a ZIP — for example a Velociraptor offline collection — can carry the analysis machine's timezone error: ZIP stores local "DOS" times, and the unzip applies the local offset again. On a UTC+10 workstation every extracted time reads ten hours early. The app therefore takes Changed (UTC) from, in order:

  1. the collection's own file metadata (results\…All Matches Metadata.json in Velociraptor collections) — chip vr;
  2. the TaskCache Tree key's LastWrite time — chip reg;
  3. the file time as extracted — chip file?, shown amber.

When extracted times disagree with an authoritative source by a consistent offset, a banner above the overview says so (the "-10:00 for 47 of 47 tasks" banner in the screenshots). The raw extracted time is kept in ExtractedModifiedUtc. RegDate is copied verbatim from the XML: it is host-local unless it carries a Z, and usually absent.

7  Scoring reference

A task is flagged at score ≥ 3. Every action of a task is evaluated (XML and registry copies), not just the first. The case window never affects scoring.

RuleSignalScore
IOCIOC / keyword hit on path, author, description, run-as, any action's command / arguments / working directory / COM class or data+3
LOLBINLauncher is a script host or living-off-the-land binary (powershell, pwsh, cmd, mshta, wscript, cscript, rundll32, regsvr32, msiexec, certutil, bitsadmin, wmic, msbuild, installutil, regasm, regsvcs, forfiles, curl, wsl, bash, conhost, hh, cmstp, odbcconf, pcalua)+2 (Microsoft tree +1)
CRADLEIEX / Invoke-Expression, download cradles, -enc with a long base64 payload, FromBase64String, hidden window, -urlcache+2
REMOTEURL or UNC share in the action+2
USERPATHRuns from a user-writable or staging location — the program, a script / binary named in the arguments, or the working directory when the program is not installed under Program Files / Windows (AppData, Temp, Users\Public, Downloads, PerfLogs, non-Microsoft ProgramData, $Recycle.Bin, the Tasks folders)+2 (Microsoft tree +1)
SYSTEMNon-Microsoft task runs as SYSTEM or with highest privileges+1
S4U PASSWORDNon-Microsoft task with a non-interactive S4U logon, or stored credentials+1
ONESHOTSingle time trigger that ends ≤ 24 h after it starts, or delete-after-expiry — the remote-push shape+1
HIDDEN BEACONNon-Microsoft task marked Hidden; non-Microsoft task repeating every ≤ 15 minutes+1 each
MALFORMED NOTTASK NOTUTF16Malformed / empty / unreadable task file; non-XML file in a Tasks folder; UTF-8 task file+2 / +2 / +1
WOW64 ATJOB JOBTask file under SysWOW64\Tasks; legacy At<n>.job; other legacy .job+2 / +3 / +1
NOSDTree key without its SD value — hidden from schtasks and the UI+3
REGONLY TREEONLYRegistered with no XML; Tree-only residue (non-Microsoft +3, Microsoft with Index ≠ 0 +2)+2 / +3
XMLONLY REGDELETEDXML with no registration; deleted registration recovered from the hive+1 each
ACTMISMATCHTaskCache's copy of the actions differs from the XML+2
context, +0MULTI more than one action · COM COM handler · DISABLED · ACCT-AUTHOR author is a DOMAIN\user account · URIMISMATCH <URI> differs from the file location · STALE routine Microsoft Tree leftover+0
Tasks under \Microsoft\ score half on LOLBIN and USERPATH — Windows ships many script-host tasks there — but are never exempt: attackers hide tasks in that tree precisely because people skip it. Legitimate admin scripts that run PowerShell with stored credentials and highest privileges score 4; that is also exactly what persistence with a stolen admin account looks like, so they are left visible.

8  Hunting playbook

Five-minute host triage

  1. Process the host, then click Flagged. Read the top rows' reasons in the detail pane.
  2. Click Non-Microsoft — usually a short list. Anything you cannot name is worth a look.
  3. Click Registry anomalies. Anything other than STALE leftovers needs an explanation.
  4. Switch to Timeline and read around your incident window; set the date filter or launch with /from: /to:.

Patterns worth knowing

  • Remote push / lateral movement: a root-level task, SYSTEM, a one-shot time trigger a few minutes after registration, launching PowerShell or cmd — LOLBIN SYSTEM ONESHOT, often REMOTE or CRADLE. Compare Registered (UTC) with the logon that created it.
  • Cleaned-up task: TREEONLY or REGDELETED — the name and the Tree LastWrite (or recovered times) may be all that is left. The same name on several hosts is a strong lead.
  • Hidden task: NOSD — present on disk and in the registry, invisible to schtasks /query.
  • XML deleted, still running: REGONLY with decoded actions.
  • Tampered task: ACTMISMATCH or URIMISMATCH.

Correlate

Task files and registry keys show what exists, not everything that happened. Pair the findings with TaskScheduler/Operational events 106 (registered), 140 (updated), 141 (deleted), 200/201 (action started / completed) and Security 4698–4702 (task created / deleted / enabled / disabled / updated) — Hayabusa-Wrapper and Login Activity Triage in the same toolkit read those — and with $UsnJrnl (MFTECmd-Wrapper) for task files created and deleted inside the window.

9  Command line & family conventions

mshta "SchedTasks-Analyzer.hta" "<inputOrCsv>" ["<outDir>"] [/auto] [/from:yyyy-MM-dd] [/to:yyyy-MM-dd]
  • <input> — a .csv (opens in the viewer) or a host folder / Tasks folder / task file (prefilled; processed with /auto).
  • <outDir> — output folder; the default is _Processed\<host>\SchedTasks next to the app. A _Processed\<host>\ outDir also names the host.
  • /auto — process immediately; if RECmd is missing and the web is reachable it is downloaded first.
  • /from: /to: — case window (UTC, inclusive): prefills the date filter and is recorded in runinfo.json; never scored.

Shared with every tool in the family:

  • Target hostname is required before processing; it is guessed from Collection-<host>-… paths or a _Processed\<host>\ outDir.
  • IOC.txt next to the app (one term per line, # comments) is merged into the IOC box at launch.
  • runinfo.json in the output folder records each run (app, version, host, input, files, case window) plus a triage summary — the DFIR-Windows-Artifact-Finder shows it per host in its inventory.
  • RECmd's raw TaskCache CSVs are kept beside the analyzer CSV in TaskCache\ for provenance.
  • The Artifact-Finder lists a Scheduled tasks row per host and launches this app with the host folder and outDir prefilled.

RegStatus RegGuid RegCreatedUtc RegLastStartUtc RegLastStopUtc RegLastResult RegTaskStateTaskCache status and the registry's times and last result (hex).

Export view → CSV writes the current filtered view with Score, Tags, Flagged, User added; Copy for case notes puts one line per task on the clipboard.

11  Limits & troubleshooting

  • "Target hostname is required" — the input path has no Collection-<host>-… segment; type the host (or launch from the Artifact-Finder, which passes it).
  • No TaskCache columns — RECmd was not found (use Download RECmd), no SOFTWARE hive sits beside the Tasks folder, or the hive could not be copied. The log says which. A dirty hive without its transaction logs is re-run without log replay and reported as a warning.
  • Live machine — needs an elevated mshta; the live hive is locked, so live runs are XML-only.
  • Network share — runs from a mapped drive or UNC path fall back to ANSI file IO for UTF-8 files; UTF-16 task files are unaffected. Copy the app locally for full fidelity.
  • Raw XML in the detail pane exists only for tasks parsed in the current session (not after Load existing CSV).
  • Not decoded: legacy .job contents, SendEmail / ShowMessage actions in the registry blob, COM CLSID names.
  • CSV in Excel — values are written unmodified and task arguments can start with -, +, = or @; open the CSV in this app or Timeline Explorer rather than Excel.
